requirement_statement.text: Definitions: sc-agent is the crates and CLIs of this repository. A CLI is one of the command-line programs decidr or sitr; `<cli>` is its name in lower case and `<CLI>` in upper case. A Logger is an sc-observability logger that a caller passes to a CLI's library entry point. The general log is the diagnostic log of one entry point (ADR-SAG-0021); decidr's is `decidr.log.jsonl` and sitr's is `sitr.log.jsonl`. A session log is the record of every session; a session is one model request with its own ULID `session_id`, and every send of that request, including busy resends, belongs to it. A link record ties one run to one session (REQ-SAG-0005). A run log is the file of link records that sits beside a session log in the same directory. To remove a log is to rotate, prune or delete it. The generated client is the Python module a consumer renders from the sc-decidr wheel's sc-compose template (REQ-SAG-0018). The client name is the consumer's product name, a constant in the generated client, and equals its `agent_role` (REQ-SAG-0004), such as `plan-anchor` or `judge-jev`. The client Logger is the Logger the generated client obtains from the wheel under the client name (REQ-SAG-0008). `<CLIENT>_LOG_ROOT` is the environment variable named by the client name uppercased with hyphens replaced by underscores. The default session files are the session files REQ-SAG-0005 names for an agent role. The client's logs are the general log the client Logger writes and the default session files.

statements.text: With no Logger injected, each CLI MUST write its general log to `~/.sc-agent/logs/<cli>.log.jsonl`.
When `<CLI>_LOG_ROOT` is set and non-empty, that CLI MUST use its value in place of `~/.sc-agent`.
When `<CLIENT>_LOG_ROOT` is set and not empty, the generated client MUST use that folder in place of `~/.sc-agent/` for its logs.
Session logs MUST be written under `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` (REQ-SAG-0005).
A session log MUST remain in `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` whatever its age.
A run log MUST remain in `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` whatever its age.
sc-agent MUST NOT contain code that removes a general log.
sc-agent MUST NOT remove a session log.
sc-agent MUST NOT remove a run log.
The Rust API MUST accept an injected general Logger.
When a Python caller requests a named Logger, the wheel MUST return a Logger built from the linked crate.
The wheel MUST NOT depend on the `sc-observability` Python package.
The source code of this project MUST NOT call any sleep function.

decisions.title: One sc-observability Logger per process, owned by the entry point; general logs and session logs in separate trees

context.text: sc-agent logs through sc-observability. The `decidr` CLI, the `sitr` CLI and the sc-decidr wheel already link the sc-observability crate. Two kinds of log exist: the general log (diagnostics, searched for issues) and session logs (the long-term record of every model query and response, analysed later and loaded into SQLite, ADR-SAG-0002).

decision.text:
**One Logger per process, owned by the entry point.** The entry point is the CLI's `main`, or, for a Python app, its sc-compose generated client.
- The entry point obtains one sc-observability `Logger`, keeps it for the life of the process and gives it to each Run it creates (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14); the Run passes it to every decision call, flushes it after each call and on exit, and never shuts down a Logger it borrowed.
- The generated client has no close operation.
- Library code never builds a Logger of its own while one is injected, and never forwards records to Python `logging`.

**The wheel exposes the crate's Logger.** The sc-decidr wheel returns the sc-observability crate's `Logger` to Python, named by the caller.
- Python may write its own records to it and gives it to the Run of its sc-decidr calls;
- Rust receives its own Logger object back, so no record crosses a bridge and the process has one queue.
- The wheel has no dependency on the `sc-observability` Python package.

**Products.** sc-agent ships three products. sc-observability is a crate linked into each, not a product.

| Product | Contains |
|---|---|
| `decidr` CLI | decidr, sc-observability |
| `sitr` CLI | sitr, sc-observability |
| sc-decidr wheel | the decidr and sitr Python APIs, sc-observability |

There is one Python wheel.
- A Python process that loads sc-agent has one copy of sc-observability and one Logger, which it injects into decidr and sitr calls alike.
- Installing the wheel always installs both APIs, whichever one the caller uses.

**Defaults.** With no Logger injected, sc-agent uses the default sc-observability Logger, which writes the general log to disk at the paths below.
- Every decision and sitr call is logged, so with nothing configured every log lands under `~/.sc-agent/` for a full audit.
- A caller that wants another general-log sink (a database, nothing) changes the sink of the Logger it injects; that is the caller's responsibility.

**Session log.** The session log is always on and is not configurable. sc-agent writes every session row in Rust through its session sink.
- No Logger sits between sc-agent and the session sink, and the session sink never receives a general-log record.
- A session sink of the same kind, opened on the run log, appends one link record `{run_id, session_id, cached}` to the run log, `runs.jsonl` beside `sessions.jsonl`, for every query that writes a session row (`cached: false`) and for every cache hit (`cached: true`); the run log is always on and never rotated or pruned either.
- The session row carries no `run_id`: runs and sessions are many-to-many, because a cache hit serves a later run from an older session.
- Each session row carries `provider` and `usage` (`null` when the reply reports none), `model_requested` (the resolved model id) and `model_answered` (the model id the response reported, `null` when no response arrived), and has no start or end time.
- Callers inject no session Logger and cannot replace the session sink.

**Paths.** The log root is `~/.sc-agent`.
- One function returns a CLI's log root: its `<CLI>_LOG_ROOT` environment override when set and non-empty (used by tests), else `~/.sc-agent`.
- The CLIs and the wheel call that function; nothing else computes a log path.
- The wheel's `sc_agent.session_rows(session_ids, *, agent_role, project=None)` is the one reader of the session-log layout: it finds the log root with the same function used to write session rows and returns, as an ok value, a map from each requested `session_id` to its row; a missing id returns `session.not_found` (category `validation`) naming the ids.
- A generated client reads session rows only through it and has no log-root argument (NFR-SAG-0004).

- Session logs are `~/.sc-agent/sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl`, and each one's run log is `runs.jsonl` in the same directory.

| Entry point | General log | Session logs |
|---|---|---|
| `decidr` CLI | `logs/decidr.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl` |
| `sitr` CLI | `logs/sitr.log.jsonl` | none |
| `plan-anchor` (generated client) | `logs/plan-anchor.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/plan-anchor/<project>/sessions.jsonl` |
| `judge-jev` (generated client) | `logs/judge-jev.log.jsonl`, holding its decidr and sitr records | `sessions/<repo>/judge-jev/<project>/sessions.jsonl` |

A wheel is not an entry point and has no row: it writes to the Logger its caller injects.
- Every entry point has a row and every cell is filled.
- The table is updated when an entry point is added.

**Session identity.**

- `agent_role` is the agent or app making the request.
- A generated client hardcodes it to its product name; it is not a user setting.
- `tool` and `tool_version` name the program that sent the query and its version: the generated client's name, or `decidr` (REQ-SAG-0004).
- They are carried by the Run the query is sent through (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14).
- `project` is the project/phase, resolved by the configuration lookup of ADR-SAG-0020 (`--project`, `SC_PROJECT`, then the config files).
- It is required and has no default; a session without one is refused with a typed error naming every place it can be set.
- Usage, help and errors call it "project/phase".

**Errors.** An error is logged once, in Rust, with the same id and fields whatever the harness, so the general logs can be searched with one set of terms.
- It is logged again only when an outer layer adds information that helps debugging.
- A failed `log.write` or `log.flush` returns the Logger's failure as an error value; nothing else handles it.
- A successful decision remains in its session row when general logging fails; the call returns the log error rather than that decision value.

context.text: sc-agent will launch decision models, LLMs, CLI agents and SDK agents. Each needs shared types, configuration, secrets, HTTP and logging, but not each other's code.

decision.text:
`sc-agent` is the bottom layer: the provider tables, `send` and `send_batch`, resends, keys, configuration, errors, logging paths and session rows.
- `sc-treesitter` (tree-sitter extraction) is over `sc-agent`.
- On top: `decidr` (the decision CLI), `sitr` (the tree-sitter CLI) and `sc-agent-py` (the one wheel, holding the decidr and sitr APIs).
- CLI agents and SDK agents get their own crates later.
- Errors are discriminated unions: every call returns `Result<T, E>`, and `E` carries the error info: at least an id and a message.
- A layer that changes an error keeps the lower error's id and message (REQ-SAG-0002).
- An error may carry more fields.
- Whether a crate has its own error type or shares one is not specified.
